align.prompt: LLM ablation baseline for as-twn-taipei / orig-llm-skeleton2grid-opus5: force re-run llm-straighten then llm-network-loop from scratch, maximizing H/V (45 deg as fallback).

transcript.note: Round 1. I built a lock table from hvSegs first (a V segment locks a column, an H segment locks a row) and found 6 fully free vertices (4,8,29,42,43,47) plus 28 half-free ones; every proposal below only uses a free axis, so none of the 53 existing H/V segments is touched. Four groups of reasoning: (a) NORTH-WEST CHAIN 8-47-4-35 was three separate skew/diagonal segments; all four vertices are free or row-free, so I collapsed the whole chain onto one shared row 7 (the median of rows 0/5/6/10), giving three new H at once. (b) COLUMN-41 SPINE: 36 and 58 are joined by a V, so translating the pair 2 cells west (43->41) keeps that V, and it lands 58 exactly above 16 once 16 slides 2 cells east along its locked row 28, so 58-16 becomes V; the same translation turns 44-58 and 16-33 into exact 45 deg. (c) DIAGONAL HUB 45: its row is free and it sits 5 columns from both 36's new column and 20's column, so row 18 makes 45-36 (+5,+5) and 45-20 (+5,-5) 45 deg simultaneously - one move, two upgrades. (d) DEGREE-1 LEAVES 42,43,29 and the near-misses 2/3, 18/37, 38, 26, 50, 55 were each aligned onto a neighbour's locked coordinate: 55 down to row 23 (34's locked row), 18+37 translated one column east so 38-18 becomes V while 18-37 V and 18-20 H both survive, 38 up one row so 38-12 becomes 45 deg, 2+3 onto the shared column 41 (column 47 was rejected in my own check because a V there would have crossed the H segment 5-6 at row 8, breaking hard rule 3), 43 to row 23 and 42 to column 43 turning two long leaf segments exactly H and V. I verified the 360 deg bearing order of every degree>=3 vertex whose neighbourhood changes (36,58,16,18,38,2,45,33,20,23,44,24,13,12,39,15,25,51,49,27) stays cyclically identical, and hand-checked the new segments for crossings and point-swallowing.

Round 2. Diagnosing the single rejection of round 1: I had asked for 2 -> (41,10), west of 18. Vertex 18 has degree 4 and its incident bearings are 38 north, 20 west, 37 south, 2 east-ish; putting 2 west of 18 would have wound 2 past 37 and past 20, so the winding-order rule rightly refused it. The admissible region for 2 is therefore the eastern half-plane of 18 (column > 44), which rules out both a shared column with 18 and my original target. Inside that region there are two competing plays: column 47 makes 2-3 and 2-18 both exactly 45 deg (+2 diagonal), while column 45 makes 2-3 an exact V (+1 H/V) and gives up the 2-18 diagonal. Since the score is lexicographic with H/V as the primary key, I take the V: 2 -> (45,10), 3 -> (45,4). Column 45 rather than 47 is deliberate - a vertical at column 47 or 46 would cross the existing horizontal segment 5-6, which runs along row 8 from column 46 to 48, and hard rule 3 forbids adding a crossing; column 45 passes just west of that segment. 3's row 4 is locked by 3-1 so only its column moves, and 2's row 10 is locked by 13-2 so only its column moves - both existing H segments survive, just longer.

Round 3. Only three segments are still unaligned: 36-23 (+3,-2), 13-38 (-4,+9) and 23-20 (-3,-8). 13-38 and 23-20 are provably stuck - 13 cannot move west past column 46 without winding 2 from its west side to its east side, 38's column is pinned by two V segments, and 20 cannot share 18's column without crossing it along their common row 13 - so 36-23 is the only one left with any room. Making it 45 deg needs a row difference of 3 instead of 2, and 23's row is locked by 23-12, whose row is in turn locked by 22-12 and 22-46. So rather than break that chain I translate the whole locked row as a rigid body: 23, 12, 22 and 46 all drop from row 21 to row 20, which preserves all three of those H segments (and the V segments 44-23, 38-23, 40-12, 17-22, 53-22, which only care about columns) and turns 36-23 into an exact (+3,-3). That shift alone would cost me the 38-12 diagonal, so 38 - whose row is free - goes up one to row 18, restoring (+2,+2), and 38-18 / 38-23 stay vertical because they only depend on column 44. I checked that the lengthened verticals 53-22 and 38-18 swallow no vertex, that the lengthened horizontals 22-46 and 22-12 cross nothing between columns 48-54 and 46-48, and that the bearing order at all five affected hubs (23 degree 5, 12, 22, 38, 36, 20, 18, 13) is cyclically unchanged. Net effect: H/V unchanged at 63, eight-direction count up by one, and the residual unaligned set shrinks to the two structurally impossible segments.

Round 4. I revisited 13-38, which I had written off as impossible. It cannot become H/V - 38's column is pinned by two V segments, and 13 cannot move west past column 46 without swapping 2 from its west to its east side - but it can become an exact 45 deg, because its column difference is fixed at -4 and 13's row is free apart from the H segment 13-2. Putting 13 on row 14 (38 sits on row 18) gives exactly (-4,+4). The obstruction is that the V segment 6-13 would then run down column 48 from row 8 to row 14 and pass straight through vertex 53 at (48,13) - swallowing a station, which hard rule 3 forbids - and it would also cross the H segment 54-53 along row 13. So I lift that whole two-vertex appendage out of the way: 53 to (48,15) and 54 to (53,15), which keeps 54-53 horizontal and 53-22 vertical while leaving column 48 clear over rows 9-13. 2 rides along to row 14 to keep 13-2 horizontal, and that is a bonus rather than a cost: 2-18 becomes (-1,-1), the last near-miss in that corner, so this one round converts both remaining fixable segments. I checked the bearing order at 13, 2, 18, 6 and 22 is cyclically unchanged (at 18, vertex 2 swings from south-east to north-east but stays inside the arc between 37 and 38, so nothing is wound past), that the lengthened vertical 6-13 and the relocated horizontal 54-53 swallow no vertex and cross nothing, and that the diagonal 13-38 stays strictly north of 2-18 over their shared column range. After this only 23-20 remains unaligned: its row difference is 7 against a column difference of 3, and every way of closing it - lifting 20/0/18 to row 17, or dropping the locked row-20 band to row 16 - destroys two 45 deg segments or swallows 38, so it is genuinely at its limit.

Round 5. Round 4 was reverted wholesale, and the reason taught me the real shape of the constraint. I had assumed the only limits on a vertex were the winding order and crossings, but hard rule 2 also freezes each vertex inside its quadrant relative to every neighbour: 2 currently sits 3 rows south of 18, so it may reach 18's row but may never cross to the north of it. That kills the plan of lifting 13-2 to row 14 (2 could not follow), which in turn is why the batch lost a horizontal and was rolled back. Reading that constraint the other way round turns it into an opportunity: 2 is allowed to land exactly on 18's row, and landing there converts 2-18 from a near-miss into a true H. So this round walks the 13-2 horizontal down to row 13 instead of up to row 14: 2 to (45,13), 13 to (48,13). That needs the 53/54 appendage out of the way first - 53 already occupies (48,13) - so 53 drops to (48,15) and 54 follows to (53,15), which keeps 54-53 horizontal and 53-22 vertical, and leaves column 48 clear over rows 9 to 13 so the lengthened V 6-13 swallows nobody. The result is one long horizontal 0-20-18-2-13 running from column 37 to column 48 along row 13, gaining an H that no amount of pushing upward could have produced. 13-38 stays unaligned: with 13 pinned to row 13 the only way to make it 45 deg is to pull 38 down to row 17, and that costs the 38-12 diagonal, so it is a wash and I am leaving the layout alone rather than churning it.

Convergence note (no moves). H/V went 53 -> 64 of 74 segments and the eight-direction count 56 -> 72 of 74 over five rounds. The two survivors are 13-38 and 23-20, and both are at a strict trade-off rather than merely hard: 13-38 has a fixed column difference of -4 (38's column is pinned by two V segments, 13 cannot cross west of 2), so making it 45 deg means pulling 38 down to row 17, which costs the 38-12 diagonal - I checked and the count comes back 64/72, unchanged. Reaching it from 13's side instead (column 47, 38 on row 16) is worse, 63/71, because it breaks the 13-2 horizontal. 23-20 needs either 20 lifted to row 17, which costs the 45-20 diagonal and makes the lengthened V 6-13 swallow 53, or the locked row-20 band dropped to row 16, which costs the 36-23 diagonal and swallows 38; the first measures 63/71. So both are genuinely at their limit under the quadrant rule, and further rounds would only churn the layout. Stopping at round 5 of the 10 allowed.
